question.text: The Musket Wars were a series of conflicts fought between the iwi, or tribes, of these Polynesian natives of New Zealand.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.leadin: This country formed an army corps with Australia that fought in the Gallipoli campaign and is honored on ANZAC Day.
swap.text: Name this country, the location of silver ferns, which are featured on its airline's planes and its coat of arms. This island country, whose capital is Wellington, is located southeast of Australia.
swap.clue: Another conflict in this country began after Hone Heke destroyed a gift he had given to James Busby, who co-wrote a document that ambiguously translated the word "sovereignty."

question.leadin: This kingdom's Law of the Splintered Paddle allowed all civilians to travel in peace.
question.text: Name this kingdom, which was ruled from ʻIolani Palace. Sanford Dole helped overthrow this kingdom's last ruler, Queen Liliʻuokalani [luh-lee-uh-wo-kuh-LAA-nee].
question.clue: An attempt to replace the Bayonet Constitution led to the overthrow of this kingdom by a group including Sanford Dole.

swap.leadin: This island chain was discovered by Polynesian explorers from the Marquesas Islands using double-hulled canoes called "Waʻa."
swap.text: Name this island chain whose traditional mythology worshipped volcanoes such as Mauna Kea ["MOH-nuh KAY-uh"] and Kilauea ["key-loh-AY-uh"].
swap.clue: This region was forcibly* annexed by the United States in 1898.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about American leaders involved in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
question.text: Nimitz also participated in this battle, which is often considered to be the turning point of the Pacific Theatre. The Aleutian Islands Campaign was intended as a diversion from this battle, where the USS Yorktown and all four Japanese aircraft carriers that took part in the battle were sunk.
question.clue: The winning side in this battle lost the (+) Yorktown, whereas the losing side of this battle lost 4 aircraft carriers.

swap.leadin: One movement of this type worships John Frum.
swap.text: Identify these religious movements, particularly prominent on Pacific Islands, in which natives assume that representatives of technologically advanced cultures must be gods due to the gifts they leave behind.
swap.clue: The Tuka movement was documented in 1885, and in 1919 G.M. Murray and F.E. Williams observed one variety of it associated with iki haveve and the Ghost Steamer, which they called Vailala Madness.

question.leadin: The successful voyage of this vessel supported the idea that contact between South America and Polynesia happened before the Europeans came.
question.text: Name the balsa wood raft that crossed the Pacific in 1947.

swap.leadin: The Catamaran likely originated from these people.
swap.text: Name these ancient ancestors of people from New Zealand, New Guinea, and Madagascar. Their namesake expansion likely began around 1500-1000BCE.

question.leadin: This country was unified in the 19th century by Tanoa Visawaqa ("ta-NO-ah vees-ah-WA-ka").
question.text: Name this country once home to a chief who was supposedly the most prolific cannibal in history, Udre-Udre ("OO-dre OO-dre"). A racist KKK composed of Australians operated in this Pacific country where an aquifer names a brand of water.
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.leadin: The second ruler of this name abolished the tapu code of conduct.
swap.text: Give this name of the ruler who won the Battle of Nuʻuanu to become the first king of a unified Hawaii.
swap.answerHtml: Kamehameha [accept Kamehameha II; accept Kamehameha I or Kamehameha the Great]
swap.clue: The third person of this name was inspired by William Richards to issue the Edict of Toleration and Declaration of Rights, which introduced a legislature and supreme court to his country.

question.text: This New Zealand prime minister, the second woman to hold the office, officially apologized to Samoa in 2002 for injustices during colonial rule. This prime minister also introduced the controversial Foreshore and Seabed Act.

swap.leadin: The signing of this document is celebrated on a February 6 holiday.
swap.text: Name this 1840 treaty signed by British representatives and native chiefs, including Hone Heke and Te Wharerahi. It is considered the founding document of a modern day island nation.
swap.clue: Instructions for this treaty were issued by Lord Normanby, and it was drafted in four days by James Busby and Lieutenant Governor William Hobson.

question.text: Scholars have suggested that only the introduction of sweet potato, which supplanted taro and yam, was sufficient to facilitate the labor needed to build many ahu and moai on this island after 1200 CE.
question.clue: The local cultivation and name of the sweet potato indicated that people in this place likely had contact with South America.

swap.text: Many residents of this island are of Tahitian descent. This island was populated following the mutiny on the HMS Bounty.
swap.clue: Police officer Gail Cox denounced the culture of sexual abuse on this island, the subject of a controversial 2004 trial that convicted six of its residents.

question.text: After the initial Moa-hunter period ended, the Classic Period began, which was characterised by the development of these hill forts.
question.clue: This fortified settlements and defensive structures of the Maori. The Flagstaff War ended with a battle at one of these places called Ruapekapeka.

swap.leadin: A leader of this expedition beat Charles Gray after Gray stole skilligolee (SKIL-ee-goh-lee) porridge and contracted dysentery.
swap.text: Name this failed 1860s expedition which is commemorated on the Dig Tree. The Irish soldier John King was the only man to successfully see this expedition to fruition.
swap.answerHtml: Burke and Wills expedition [or answers describing the expedition of Robert O'Hara Burke and William John Wills; or Victorian Exploring Expedition]

question.leadin: An airbase called Henderson Field was a critical facility on this island, where ships coming in from the northwest were often sunk in "The Slot," or Ironbottom Sound.
question.text: Name this island, where U.S. and Japanese forces fought as the year 1942 gave way to 1943.
question.clue: The naval battle named for this island in the Solomon Islands occurred after the United States captured Henderson Airfield. The early battles on this island had the codename Operation Watchtower, and it was the first major offensive by the Allies against Japan.

swap.text: This favorite wife of Kamehameha, on the other hand, converted to Protestantism and embarked on a campaign of destroying sacred Hawaiian sites and promoting literacy so that Hawaiians could read the Bible.

question.leadin: Native speakers of this language started to use the word palapala in the 1820s to refer to the body of written knowledge produced with the help of Christian missionaries.
question.text: Name this language. The nineteenth-century historians Davida Malo and "Kepelino" both wrote in this language, and Lorrin A. Thurston wrote a constitution in this language.

swap.leadin: Identify the following relating to the problem of longitude, FTPE.
swap.text: The K-1 clock made by Larcum Kendall, based on the design of Harrison, served as an aide for this British captain who was killed by Hawaiians in February of 1779.
swap.clue: The naturalists Daniel Solander and Joseph Banks accompanied this man on that voyage, during which this explorer visited Botany Bay.
